mots.sens: The term 'minḥah' refers to an offering or gift made to God, often in the form of agricultural products. It evokes the idea of devotion and acknowledgment towards God, emphasizing that everything we have belongs to Him. In this context, the grain offering symbolizes simplicity and humility, while being an act of faith and gratitude.

The word 'shemen' means oil and is often associated with consecration and anointing. In the context of offerings, oil represents the presence and action of the Holy Spirit, bringing a spiritual dimension to the offering. It also underscores the importance of quality and purity in our gifts to God.

The term 'levonah' refers to incense, which is used in worship rituals to symbolize prayer and adoration. When burned, incense releases a pleasant fragrance that is perceived as a pleasing offering to God. Spiritually, this represents how our prayers ascend to Him, creating a connection between heaven and earth.
